## Genetic mosaicism practical

This practical is designed for **RStudio Server running through Biowulf OnDemand**.
Shared workshop reference files, test data, and Singularity container images are provided
on the Biowulf shared filesystem. Each participant writes intermediate and final results
to a personal working directory.

**How to use this document:** Work through the sections in order. R code is in `{r}`
chunks and Linux commands are in `{bash}` chunks. For a Bash chunk, click the green
Run button for the chunk. The commands run on the Biowulf compute node allocated to
RStudio Server.

### 1. Set up

#### Workshop resources and participant working area

Shared workshop resources are located at:

```text
/data/DCEG_shared/statgen_workshop_2026/statgen_workshop_tutorial/DCEG_mosaicism_workshop
```

Participant-specific working files are stored under:

```text
/data/<Biowulf-username>/statgen_workshop_2026/session8/mosaicism
```

The shared directory is used for input resources; the participant directory is used for
files generated during the practical.

#### Define paths

```{r}
# Shared workshop resources
workshop_dir <- "/data/DCEG_shared/statgen_workshop_2026/statgen_workshop_tutorial/DCEG_mosaicism_workshop"
ref_dir <- file.path(workshop_dir, "ref_files")
sig_dir <- file.path(workshop_dir, "sig_files")
test_dir <- file.path(workshop_dir, "test_set")

# Singularity images used in the 2026 workshop
bcftools_sif <- file.path(sig_dir, "bcftools_1.20-20240927.sif")
eagle_sif <- file.path(sig_dir, "eagle_1.16-20221221.sif")

# Participant-specific working area
user_name <- Sys.getenv("USER")
if (!nzchar(user_name)) {
  stop("Biowulf USER environment variable is not set.")
}

analysis_dir <- file.path(
  "/data",
  user_name,
  "statgen_workshop_2026",
  "session8",
  "mosaicism"
)

# Reference files
ref <- file.path(ref_dir, "human_g1k_v37.fasta")
maps <- file.path(ref_dir, "genetic_map_hg19_withX.txt.gz")
kgp_pfx <- file.path(ref_dir, "ALL.chr")
kgp_sfx <- ".phase3_integrated.20130502.genotypes"
cnp <- file.path(ref_dir, "cnp.grch37.bed")
cyto <- file.path(ref_dir, "cytoBand.hg19.txt.gz")
ref_phase <- file.path(ref_dir, "ALL.phase3_integrated.20130502.sites.bcf")

# 2026 workshop test set
genome_studio_file <- file.path(
  test_dir,
  "full_data_table_test_set.txt"
)

# Regions used by MOChA
mhc_reg <- "6:27486711-33448264"
kir_reg <- "19:54574747-55504099"
rule <- "GRCh37"

# Participant output directories
temp_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "temp")
to_bcf <- file.path(analysis_dir, "to_bcf")
phasing <- file.path(analysis_dir, "phasing")
phasing_by_chrs <- file.path(phasing, "by_chrs")
mocha <- file.path(analysis_dir, "mocha")
plots <- file.path(analysis_dir, "plots")
logs <- file.path(analysis_dir, "logs")
circos <- file.path(analysis_dir, "circos")
baf_regress <- file.path(analysis_dir, "baf_regress")
analysis_bin <- file.path(analysis_dir, "bin")

# MOChA plotting script used in the 2026 workshop
mocha_plot_script <- file.path(
  workshop_dir,
  "bin",
  "mocha_plot.09.27.24.R"
)

# Use the original shared workshop Circos script.
circos_script <- file.path(workshop_dir, "circos", "plot_mosaic_circos.R")
if (file.access(circos_script, 4) != 0) {
  stop("Shared Circos script is not readable: ", circos_script)
}

# Create participant output directories
for (d in c(
  analysis_dir,
  analysis_bin,
  temp_dir,
  to_bcf,
  phasing,
  phasing_by_chrs,
  mocha,
  plots,
  logs,
  circos,
  baf_regress
)) {
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

# Make paths available to Bash chunks
Sys.setenv(
  WORKSHOP_DIR = workshop_dir,
  REF_DIR = ref_dir,
  SIG_DIR = sig_dir,
  TEST_DIR = test_dir,
  ANALYSIS_DIR = analysis_dir,
  REF = ref,
  GENOME_STUDIO_FILE = genome_studio_file,
  MAPS = maps,
  KGP_PFX = kgp_pfx,
  KGP_SFX = kgp_sfx,
  CNP = cnp,
  CYTO = cyto,
  REF_PHASE = ref_phase,
  MHC_REG = mhc_reg,
  KIR_REG = kir_reg,
  RULE = rule,
  TEMP_DIR = temp_dir,
  TO_BCF = to_bcf,
  PHASING = phasing,
  PHASING_BY_CHRS = phasing_by_chrs,
  MOCHA = mocha,
  PLOTS = plots,
  LOGS = logs,
  CIRCOS = circos,
  BAF_REGRESS = baf_regress,
  ANALYSIS_BIN = analysis_bin,
  BCFTOOLS_SIF = bcftools_sif,
  EAGLE_SIF = eagle_sif,
  MOCHA_PLOT_SCRIPT = mocha_plot_script,
  CIRCOS_SCRIPT = circos_script
)
```

#### Verify the setup

This check confirms that the shared resources and required software files are available
and that the participant working directory is writable.

```{r}
required_files <- c(
  reference = ref,
  genetic_map = maps,
  cnp = cnp,
  cytoband = cyto,

)

check <- data.frame(
  file = unname(required_files),
  exists = file.exists(required_files),
  row.names = names(required_files),

check

    "One or more required workshop files are missing:\n",
```

### 2. Containerized software on Biowulf

Biowulf provides Singularity for running containerized software. Each Bash chunk that
uses Singularity loads the module explicitly.

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity
singularity --version
```

#### Test the bcftools container

The 2026 practical uses **bcftools 1.20**, which includes the `BAFregress` plugin used
for the contamination check below.

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \
  bcftools --version
```

#### Test the EAGLE2 container

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$EAGLE_SIF" \
  eagle --help >/dev/null

echo "EAGLE2 container is accessible."
```

### 3. Converting the GenomeStudio CNV table to BCF

The GenomeStudio table is converted to BCF with `bcftools +gtc2vcf`, then sorted and
normalized against the reference genome. The resulting BCF is the input for phasing
and can also be used for the contamination check.

#### Run `bcftools +gtc2vcf`

The 2026 test input is:

```text
/data/DCEG_shared/statgen_workshop_2026/statgen_workshop_tutorial/DCEG_mosaicism_workshop/test_set/full_data_table_test_set.txt
```

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \
  bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail

    bcftools +gtc2vcf --no-version -Ou \
      --genome-studio "$GENOME_STUDIO_FILE" \
      -f "$REF" | \
    bcftools sort -Ou -T "$TEMP_DIR" | \
    bcftools norm --no-version -Ob \
      -o "$TO_BCF/samples.bcf" \
      -c x -f "$REF"

    bcftools index -f \
      "$TO_BCF/samples.bcf" \
      -o "$TO_BCF/samples.bcf.csi"
  '
```


```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
ls -lh "$TO_BCF"
```

Expected files:

```text
samples.bcf
samples.bcf.csi
```

### 4. Contamination check using BAFRegress

[BAFRegress](https://genome.sph.umich.edu/wiki/BAFRegress) uses B-allele frequency
and population allele-frequency information to estimate sample contamination. Here it
is applied to the BCF generated in the previous step.

#### Verify the BAFRegress plugin

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \
  bcftools plugin -l | grep -i BAF
```

The output should include `BAFregress`.

#### Run BAFRegress

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
echo "Running BAFRegress..."
echo "Input BCF: $TO_BCF/samples.bcf"
echo "AF reference: $REF_PHASE"
echo "Output: $BAF_REGRESS/baf_regress.txt"

module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \
  bcftools +BAFregress "$TO_BCF/samples.bcf" \
    --af "$REF_PHASE" \
    -e "$BAF_REGRESS/baf_regress.txt"
```

#### Check the BAFRegress output

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
ls -lh "$BAF_REGRESS"
cat "$BAF_REGRESS/baf_regress.txt"
```

### 5. Phasing using EAGLE2

EAGLE2 phases the genotype data chromosome by chromosome. During the practical,
chromosomes 1-22 and X are submitted as separate Slurm jobs so they can run in parallel.

#### Prepare the EAGLE2 phasing script

The phasing script is created in the participant's working directory and is used by the
23 Slurm jobs below.

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
cat > "$ANALYSIS_BIN/phasing.sh" <<'PHASING_SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

chr="$1"
maps="$2"
kgp_pfx="$3"
kgp_sfx="$4"
analysis_dir="$5"
eagle2_sif="$6"
bcftools_sif="$7"

to_bcf="$analysis_dir/to_bcf"
phasing_by_chrs="$analysis_dir/phasing/by_chrs"

ref_bcf="${kgp_pfx}${chr}${kgp_sfx}.bcf"
out_prefix="${phasing_by_chrs}/samples.chr${chr}"

if [ ! -f "$to_bcf/samples.bcf" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: target BCF not found: $to_bcf/samples.bcf" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "$ref_bcf" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: reference BCF not found: $ref_bcf" >&2
  exit 1
fi

module load singularity
mkdir -p "$phasing_by_chrs"

echo "========================================"
echo "EAGLE2 phasing chromosome $chr"
echo "Reference: $ref_bcf"
echo "Target:    $to_bcf/samples.bcf"
echo "Output:    ${out_prefix}.bcf"
echo "========================================"

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$eagle2_sif" \
  eagle \
    --geneticMapFile "$maps" \
    --outPrefix "$out_prefix" \
    --vcfRef "$ref_bcf" \
    --vcfTarget "$to_bcf/samples.bcf" \
    --vcfOutFormat b \
    --noImpMissing \
    --outputUnphased \
    --chrom "$chr" \
    --pbwtIters 3 \
    --numThreads "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK:-2}"

# Index the phased BCF with the workshop bcftools 1.20 image.
singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$bcftools_sif" \
  bcftools index -f "$out_prefix.bcf"

echo "Finished chromosome $chr"
PHASING_SCRIPT

chmod +x "$ANALYSIS_BIN/phasing.sh"
echo "Created: $ANALYSIS_BIN/phasing.sh"
```

#### Verify the reference BCFs for chromosomes 1-22 and X

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
missing=0
for chr in $(seq 1 22) X; do
  ref_bcf="${KGP_PFX}${chr}${KGP_SFX}.bcf"
  if [ -f "$ref_bcf" ]; then
    echo "OK: chr${chr}"
  else
    echo "MISSING: chr${chr} -> $ref_bcf"
    missing=1
  fi
done

if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "One or more chromosome reference BCFs are missing. No EAGLE2 jobs were submitted."
  exit 1
fi
```

#### Submit EAGLE2 for chromosomes 1-22 and X

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
test -f "$EAGLE_SIF" || { echo "ERROR: EAGLE2 SIF not found: $EAGLE_SIF"; exit 1; }
test -f "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" || { echo "ERROR: bcftools SIF not found: $BCFTOOLS_SIF"; exit 1; }
test -f "$TO_BCF/samples.bcf" || { echo "ERROR: target BCF not found: $TO_BCF/samples.bcf"; exit 1; }

: > "$LOGS/phasing_jobs.tsv"
for chr in $(seq 1 22) X; do
  job_id=$(sbatch --parsable --cpus-per-task=2 --mem=8g --time=01:00:00 \
    --job-name="session8_eagle_chr${chr}" \
    -o "$LOGS/eagle2_chr${chr}.out" \
    -e "$LOGS/eagle2_chr${chr}.err" \
    "$ANALYSIS_BIN/phasing.sh" \
    "$chr" \
    "$MAPS" \
    "$KGP_PFX" \
    "$KGP_SFX" \
    "$ANALYSIS_DIR" \
    "$EAGLE_SIF" \
    "$BCFTOOLS_SIF")
  job_id="${job_id%%;*}"
  printf "%s\t%s\n" "$chr" "$job_id" >> "$LOGS/phasing_jobs.tsv"
  echo "Submitted chromosome $chr as job $job_id"
done
```

This submits **23 Slurm jobs**: chromosomes 1 through 22 and X.

#### Monitor the EAGLE2 jobs

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
job_ids=$(cut -f2 "$LOGS/phasing_jobs.tsv" | paste -sd, -)
while [ -n "$(squeue -h -j "$job_ids" -o '%i' 2>/dev/null)" ]; do
  squeue -h -j "$job_ids" -o '%i %T %M %R'
  sleep 15
done
# Allow a short interval for completed-job accounting to become available.
for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
  sacct -X -n -P -j "$job_ids" --format=JobIDRaw,State,ExitCode > "$LOGS/phasing_accounting.tsv"
  if awk -F'|' 'NF >= 3 {n++; if ($2 != "COMPLETED" || $3 != "0:0") bad++} END {exit !(n == 23 && bad == 0)}' "$LOGS/phasing_accounting.tsv"; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done
cat "$LOGS/phasing_accounting.tsv"
awk -F'|' 'NF >= 3 {n++; if ($2 != "COMPLETED" || $3 != "0:0") bad++} END {exit !(n == 23 && bad == 0)}' "$LOGS/phasing_accounting.tsv"
```

This chunk waits for all 23 submitted jobs and requires successful Slurm exit codes before continuing.

#### Verify all phased BCF files and indexes

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
missing=0
for chr in $(seq 1 22) X; do
  f="$PHASING_BY_CHRS/samples.chr${chr}.bcf"
  if [ -f "$f" ] && [ -f "${f}.csi" ]; then
    echo "OK: chr${chr}"
  else
    echo "MISSING: chr${chr} -> $f or ${f}.csi"
    missing=1
  fi
done

if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "One or more phased BCF files are missing. Check $LOGS/eagle2_chr*.err and .out before continuing."
  exit 1
fi
```

#### Check results under `phasing/by_chrs/`

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
ls -lh "$PHASING_BY_CHRS"
```

Expected files include `samples.chr1.bcf` through `samples.chr22.bcf`, the chrX BCF,
and the corresponding `.csi` index files.

### 6. Concatenating phased output into a single BCF file

The chromosome-specific phased BCFs are concatenated into one BCF for downstream MOChA
analysis.

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \
  bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail

    bcftools concat --no-version -Ob \
      "$PHASING_BY_CHRS"/samples.chr{1..22}.bcf \
      "$PHASING_BY_CHRS"/samples.chrX.bcf \
      -o "$PHASING/samples.pgt.bcf"

    bcftools index --force \
      "$PHASING/samples.pgt.bcf" \
      -o "$PHASING/samples.pgt.bcf.csi"
  '
```

#### Check results under `phasing/`

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
ls -lh "$PHASING"
```

Expected files include:

```text
samples.pgt.bcf
samples.pgt.bcf.csi
```

### 7. mCA detection using MOChA

MOChA analyzes the phased BCF together with the reference resources to identify mosaic
chromosomal alterations (mCAs), including mosaic gains, deletions, and copy-neutral loss
of heterozygosity (CN-LOH).

#### Run `bcftools +mocha`

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

singularity exec \
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \
  bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail

    bcftools +mocha \
      --genome "$RULE" \
      --no-version \
      --output "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
      --output-type b \
      --calls "$MOCHA/samples.calls.tsv" \
      --stats "$MOCHA/samples.stats.tsv" \
      --ucsc-bed "$MOCHA/samples.ucsc.bed" \
      --cnp "$CNP" \
      --mhc "$MHC_REG" \
      --kir "$KIR_REG" \
      "$PHASING/samples.pgt.bcf"

    bcftools index --force \
      "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
      --output "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf.csi"
  '
```

#### Check MOChA results

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
ls -lh "$MOCHA"
```

Expected files include `samples.calls.tsv`, `samples.stats.tsv`, `samples.ucsc.bed`,
`samples.as.bcf`, and its `.csi` index.

#### Display MOChA calls

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
cat "$MOCHA/samples.calls.tsv"
```

```{r}
mocha_calls <- read.delim(
  file.path(mocha, "samples.calls.tsv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
if (interactive()) View(mocha_calls) else print(mocha_calls)
```

### 8. Plotting mCAs

The workshop uses `mocha_plot.09.27.24.R` to visualize selected MOChA calls.

#### Verify required R packages

The workshop R environment should already contain the packages used by the plotting
script.

```{r}
needed <- c("optparse", "reshape2", "data.table", "ggplot2", "circlize")
missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]

if (length(missing) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The following R packages are missing: ",
    paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
    ". Please install them before continuing."
  )
}
```

#### Prepare a bcftools wrapper and generate the five mCA plots

The MOChA plotting script calls `bcftools` from the system PATH. The wrapper below makes
the workshop's bcftools 1.20 container available as that `bcftools` command.

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
module load singularity

BCFTOOLS_WRAPPER="$ANALYSIS_BIN/bcftools"
SINGULARITY_BIN="$(command -v singularity)"

cat > "$BCFTOOLS_WRAPPER" <<BCFTOOLS_WRAPPER_SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

exec "$SINGULARITY_BIN" exec \\
  --bind /data/$USER:/data/$USER \\
  --bind /data/DCEG_shared:/data/DCEG_shared \\
  "$BCFTOOLS_SIF" \\
  bcftools "\$@"
BCFTOOLS_WRAPPER_SCRIPT

chmod +x "$BCFTOOLS_WRAPPER"
export PATH="$ANALYSIS_BIN:$PATH"

command -v bcftools
bcftools --version

echo
echo "Generating mCA plots..."

Rscript --vanilla "$MOCHA_PLOT_SCRIPT" \
  --mocha \
  --stats "$MOCHA/samples.stats.tsv" \
  --vcf "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
  --png "$PLOTS/S5.png" \
  --samples S5 \
  --regions 11:0-47350287 \
  --cytoband "$CYTO"

Rscript --vanilla "$MOCHA_PLOT_SCRIPT" \
  --mocha \
  --stats "$MOCHA/samples.stats.tsv" \
  --vcf "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
  --png "$PLOTS/S8.png" \
  --samples S8 \
  --regions 9:0-33487198 \
  --cytoband "$CYTO"

Rscript --vanilla "$MOCHA_PLOT_SCRIPT" \
  --mocha \
  --stats "$MOCHA/samples.stats.tsv" \
  --vcf "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
  --png "$PLOTS/S9.png" \
  --samples S9 \
  --regions 13:32064883-54917256 \
  --cytoband "$CYTO"

Rscript --vanilla "$MOCHA_PLOT_SCRIPT" \
  --mocha \
  --stats "$MOCHA/samples.stats.tsv" \
  --vcf "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
  --png "$PLOTS/S10.png" \
  --samples S10 \
  --regions 20:31144462-63025520 \
  --cytoband "$CYTO"

Rscript --vanilla "$MOCHA_PLOT_SCRIPT" \
  --mocha \
  --stats "$MOCHA/samples.stats.tsv" \
  --vcf "$MOCHA/samples.as.bcf" \
  --png "$PLOTS/S6.png" \
  --samples S6 \
  --regions 10:84111105-85108139 \
  --cytoband "$CYTO"

echo
echo "Generated plots:"
ls -lh "$PLOTS"/S5.png \
       "$PLOTS"/S6.png \
       "$PLOTS"/S8.png \
       "$PLOTS"/S9.png \
       "$PLOTS"/S10.png
```

#### Display mCA plots

##### Constitutional duplication on chr10

- Abnormal cell fraction = 73%
- Characterized by e^LRR > 1; the AB BAF band splits into two bands.

```{r, out.width="600px", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots, "S6.png"))
```

##### Mosaic deletion on chr13

- Abnormal cell fraction = 20.3%
- Characterized by e^LRR < 1; the AB BAF band splits into two bands.

```{r, out.width="600px", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots, "S9.png"))
```

##### Three mCAs on chr9p

The three calls overlap in genomic space but have different inferred cell fractions.
They illustrate how multiple mCAs can contribute to a complex BAF pattern in the same
chromosomal region.

- Blue: CN-LOH in 40.87% of cells; e^LRR is approximately 1 and the AB BAF band splits into two.
- Green: CN-LOH in 15.21% of cells.
- Orange: deletion in 13.82% of cells; e^LRR < 1 and the AB BAF band splits into two.

```{r, out.width="600px", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots, "S8.png"))
```

### 9. Circos plot illustrating autosomal mCAs

For the 2026 workshop, we use the [`mosaic-event-circos`](https://github.com/NCI-CGR/mosaic-event-circos/)
R script to visualize autosomal mosaic events.

The plotting script and example data are read directly from the shared workshop
`circos/` directory.

The example files are stored in the shared workshop `circos/` directory. The generated
images and summary files are written to the participant-specific `$CIRCOS` directory.

#### Run Circos: three event types

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
test -r "$CIRCOS_SCRIPT" || { echo "ERROR: Shared Circos script is not readable"; exit 1; }
test -f "$WORKSHOP_DIR/circos/example_data/mosaic_events_autosomal.synthetic.3types.txt" || { echo "ERROR: 3-type Circos input not found"; exit 1; }

echo "Running Circos (three event types)..."
Rscript "$CIRCOS_SCRIPT" \
  --input="$WORKSHOP_DIR/circos/example_data/mosaic_events_autosomal.synthetic.3types.txt" \
  --output-prefix="$CIRCOS/mosaic_events_autosomal.circos" \
  --genome=hg38
```

#### Run Circos: four event types

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
test -f "$WORKSHOP_DIR/circos/example_data/mosaic_events_autosomal.synthetic.4types.txt" || { echo "ERROR: 4-type Circos input not found"; exit 1; }

Rscript "$CIRCOS_SCRIPT" \
  --input="$WORKSHOP_DIR/circos/example_data/mosaic_events_autosomal.synthetic.4types.txt" \
  --output-prefix="$CIRCOS/mosaic_events_autosomal.circos2" \
  --genome=hg38 \
  --types=Gain,CN-LOH,Loss,Undetermined
```

#### Check Circos output

```{bash}
set -euo pipefail
ls -lh "$CIRCOS"
```

Expected image files include:

```text
mosaic_events_autosomal.circos.png
mosaic_events_autosomal.circos.pdf
mosaic_events_autosomal.circos2.png
mosaic_events_autosomal.circos2.pdf
```

Additional TSV summary files are also produced by the script.

#### Display the Circos plots

- Green: mosaic gain
- Blue: mosaic CN-LOH
- Red: mosaic loss

```{r, out.width="600px", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(circos, "mosaic_events_autosomal.circos.png"))
```

```{r, out.width="600px", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(circos, "mosaic_events_autosomal.circos2.png"))
```
